subject: pe
topicName: Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport

cards.front: What should you know about engagement patterns?
cards.back: The ways in which different groups of people participate (or don't participate) in physical activity and sport. These patterns vary significantly based on personal, social and cultural factors.

cards.front: What should you know about key point?
cards.back: The process of socialisation means that children learn attitudes and behaviours from their family. A child raised in a sporty family is far more likely to participate in sport than one whose family has no interest in physical activity. This influence is especially strong in early childhood.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — engagement patterns in physical activity and sport?
cards.back: 1. For Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
Lack of local facilities, cost, transport (e.g. Primary school sport programmes, free taster sessions)
Peer pressure, body image, competing interests (e.g. Youth-focused sessions, social sport, StreetGames)
Time pressures, work, family commitments (e.g. Flexible timetables, lunchtime sessions, workplace sport)
Physical limitations, fear of injury, isolation (e.g. Masters events, adapted activities, walking groups)
Cannot afford fees, kit, transport (e.g. Lower participation in fee-paying sports)
Few facilities in deprived areas (e.g. Reduced access to quality provision)
Less awareness of sport benefits (e.g. Lower prioritisation of physical activity)
Long/irregular working hours (e.g. Less time available for sport)
No safe outdoor space nearby (e.g. Fewer informal play opportunities)

Students often list barriers without suggesting solutions. Wrong: "Poor people can't afford sport." Correct: "Low-income families may not be able to afford club membership fees and kit. This can be addressed through subsidised access and equipment recycling schemes."

Students often think commercialisation has only benefited sport. Wrong: Commercialisation has only benefited sport Correct: While commercialisation brings funding and media coverage, it can also lead to corruption, loss of tradition, pressure on athletes, and inequality between funded and unfunded sports.
6 marks: Explain how engagement patterns in physical activity and sport affects sporting performance.
